minutes.headline: Commissioners reworked the pitch for a ~$47M PFAS treatment plant loan ahead of a town vote
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners spent most of this meeting line-editing the PowerPoint that will be used to ask voters to approve roughly $47 million in SRF loan and bond financing for a PFAS/iron-manganese water treatment plant, debating which points were fact versus hypothetical and cutting or adding slides. They also discussed a dispute with the Woodlands over a kayak rack (tabled), fielded a resident's pointed questions about how the SRF grant application was submitted months after the board had voted not to apply, and covered routine water-main leak repairs, a proposed PVC pipe cost-saving trial, and mailer logistics for the special town meeting.

what_happened.line: Commissioners revised the slide presentation for a special town meeting vote on financing a PFAS/iron-manganese water treatment plant, separating factual points from hypothetical ones and agreeing to finish edits by email rather than another meeting.
A commissioner found the loan amount cited for a 2024 zero-interest loan article did not match the figure shown on the current slide, and the presentation will be corrected before the vote.
A resident asked why the district applied for state revolving fund financing months after commissioners had voted not to, and why commissioners were not told until December; no vote followed.
The board tabled review of a dispute with the Woodlands neighborhood over a kayak rack until members can read the attorney correspondence.
Commissioners approved a one-time trial of PVC pipe instead of the district's standard ductile iron on a current installation, after staff quoted it at roughly half the cost.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at a special town meeting to approve loan and bond financing for the treatment plant, and the slides revised at this meeting are what they will be shown when they vote.

How that financing is structured (state revolving fund loan versus bonding) affects what water bills look like for years afterward, which is why commissioners were still correcting figures on the comparison slides.

The unresolved timeline question -- an SRF application submitted after a vote not to apply, disclosed to commissioners months later -- touches on how the board's own process is explained to voters before they're asked to approve the financing.
